places.name: Thomson’s Toronto studio

places.access: Historic studio; this record does not establish a visitable site.

trinity.title: Cowboy Junkies · The Trinity Session Reissued
trinity.evidence: The band describes recording at Holy Trinity on 27 November 1987.

sharon.title: Cowboy Junkies · Sharon, the lost album
sharon.evidence: Michael Timmins identifies three days at Sharon Temple in April 1989.

fly.title: Rush · Fly by Night
fly.evidence: Album history identifies Toronto Sound on Overlea Boulevard and the subsequent Caress of Steel sessions. Liner notes confirm recording and mixing.

2112.title: Rush · 2112
2112.evidence: Album history and liner notes identify recording and mixing at Toronto Sound, with Terry Brown.

stage.title: Rush · All the World’s a Stage
stage.evidence: Liner notes identify live recording at Massey Hall on 11–13 June 1976 and mixing at Toronto Sound.

wind.title: AGO · Conserving The West Wind
wind.evidence: The AGO distinguishes the outdoor sketch from the large canvas painted in a Toronto studio during winter 1916–17.

manse.title: Leaskdale Manse · The Manse
manse.evidence: The historic-site page reproduces a plaque naming both novels as written in this house. The plaque’s 1916 date for House of Dreams is not used as a publication date.

diviners.title: York University · Margaret Laurence
diviners.evidence: The archives biography states that most of The Diviners was written at the Otonabee River cabin during summers 1971–73.

thornhill.title: Thornhill Historical Society · The Group of Seven in Thornhill
thornhill.evidence: Identifies The Tangled Garden at Four Elms in 1916 and My Garden, Thornhill at Lismer’s John Street home around 1916. Both artists became Group of Seven members.

secret-path.title: Gord Downie · Secret Path
secret-path.evidence: Identifies recording sessions at the Bathouse in Bath during November and December 2013.

away-mine.title: Gord Downie · Away Is Mine
away-mine.evidence: Describes Bathouse sessions beginning 17 July 2017 with Josh Finlayson and Nyles Spencer.

man-machine.title: Universal Music Canada · Man Machine Poem announcement
man-machine.evidence: Identifies the Bathouse recording location, producers Kevin Drew and Dave Hamelin, and Gord Downie as the band’s vocalist and guitarist. Announces release on 17 June 2016.

alanis.title: Alanis · recording history (secondary source)
alanis.evidence: Identifies Distortion Studios, Ottawa, and September–December 1990 recording. The cited RPM issue dated 6 July 1991 could only be checked through indexed excerpts; the full scan was inaccessible. Original liner-note verification remains pending.

backbone.title: Canadian Songwriters Hall of Fame · Let Your Backbone Slide (French)
backbone.evidence: Identifies production at Don Valley Sounds in Markham by Anthony and Peter Davis, and the single’s 1989 album context.

works.title: The Trinity Session
works.creator: Cowboy Junkies
works.description: A church becomes a recording room. Cowboy Junkies describe gathering around a single microphone at Holy Trinity and capturing the album in one day.
works.aside: This connection documents recording, not where every song was written.

works.title: The West Wind
works.creator: Tom Thomson
works.description: A northern landscape took its final, large-scale form in Toronto. The AGO identifies Thomson’s city studio as the place where he painted the canvas over the winter of 1916–17.
works.aside: The outdoor sketch and the finished canvas belong to different places. This entry concerns the canvas.

works.title: Anne of the Island
works.creator: L. M. Montgomery
works.date: By 1915 · exact writing dates not specified
works.description: Anne’s world continued to grow in rural Ontario. The historic-site account names Anne of the Island among the works Montgomery wrote while living at Leaskdale Manse.
works.aside: The novel’s fictional geography is distinct from its documented writing location.

works.creator: Rush
works.description: An ambitious album takes shape on Overlea Boulevard. Rush’s own history identifies Toronto Sound as the recording site, with Terry Brown working alongside the band.
works.aside: The band’s writing process preceded the studio sessions; this pin represents recording and mixing.

works.title: Sharon
works.creator: Cowboy Junkies
works.description: Three cold spring days in a wooden temple produced an album that remained shelved for decades. Michael Timmins identifies Sharon Temple as the setting for the 1989 sessions.
works.aside: The date shown is the recording date, not the much later release.

works.title: Fly by Night
works.creator: Rush
works.description: A new chapter in Rush’s sound was recorded and mixed at Toronto Sound Studios. The band’s album history places the studio on Toronto’s Overlea Boulevard.
works.aside: The listed year is the release year. Exact session dates are not established by the cited page.

works.title: All the World’s a Stage
works.creator: Rush
works.description: Three nights at Massey Hall became Rush’s first live album. Its liner notes preserve both the recording venue and the later mixing connection to Toronto Sound.
works.aside: A live recording is a creation event for the album; it is not the origin of the performed compositions.

works.title: Anne’s House of Dreams
works.creator: L. M. Montgomery
works.description: A second Anne novel connects back to the same Ontario home. Leaskdale Manse’s historical account explicitly identifies Anne’s House of Dreams as a work written here.
works.aside: The plaque uses 1916; its meaning requires clarification. The timeline uses that source date provisionally, not as a publication claim.

works.title: Caress of Steel
works.creator: Rush
works.description: Toronto Sound connects several stages of Rush’s early discography. The band’s Fly by Night history also names Caress of Steel among the albums recorded at the studio.
works.aside: This entry relies on the band’s retrospective studio history; exact session dates remain unspecified.

works.title: The Diviners
works.creator: Margaret Laurence
works.description: A cabin beside the Otonabee River became a working retreat. York University’s archives identify it as the place where Laurence wrote most of The Diviners over three summers.
works.aside: The evidence supports a substantial part of the writing, not the entire novel or its first idea.

works.title: The Tangled Garden
works.creator: J. E. H. MacDonald
works.description: A garden in Thornhill became a landmark painting. The local historical society places its creation at MacDonald’s Four Elms home.
works.aside: Created before the Group of Seven’s formation in 1920; attributed to MacDonald individually.

works.title: My Garden, Thornhill
works.creator: Arthur Lismer
works.description: Lismer’s own garden joins the atlas. The historical society identifies his John Street home as the painting’s creation site.
works.aside: The date is approximate. This is an individual work by a future Group of Seven member.

works.title: Man Machine Poem
works.creator: The Tragically Hip
works.date: Released June 2016 · session dates unspecified here
works.description: The Hip recorded this album at their Bathouse studio with Kevin Drew and Dave Hamelin producing.
works.aside: The year is the release year, not a verified session date. This connection does not claim every song was written here.

works.title: Secret Path
works.creator: Gord Downie
works.description: Downie’s songs about Chanie Wenjack were recorded at the Bathouse. The project remembers the Indigenous child who died while trying to return home after escaping a residential school.
works.aside: This entry locates the album sessions, not Chanie Wenjack’s journey or Jeff Lemire’s illustration work.

works.title: Away Is Mine
works.creator: Gord Downie
works.description: Downie brought songs developed with Josh Finlayson to the Bathouse, working with engineer Nyles Spencer to shape the recordings.
works.aside: The album’s later release is separate from these 2017 sessions. Writing began before the studio work.

works.title: Alanis
works.creator: Alanis Morissette
works.description: Before Jagged Little Pill, Morissette recorded her debut album in Ottawa with Leslie Howe. The published recording history identifies Distortion Studios.
works.aside: Secondary-source entry: original liner-note or full contemporary-report verification remains pending. The album was released in 1991.

works.title: Let Your Backbone Slide
works.creator: Maestro Fresh Wes
works.description: Maestro’s breakthrough connects to Markham. The Canadian Songwriters Hall of Fame locates production at Don Valley Sounds with Anthony and Peter Davis.
works.aside: The source establishes production at the studio; it does not establish the song’s initial writing location.
